_comment: Team settings. The SessionStart hook keeps each researcher's CLAUDE.md, skills and shared findings current. Researchers work on their own branch (researchers/<name>), but shared updates land on main -- so a plain 'git pull' would pull only their own branch and they would silently drift. This fetches and merges origin/main into whatever branch they are on. If the merge cannot be done cleanly it aborts, leaving the working tree untouched rather than dropping conflict markers in front of a non-coder; the team-sync skill then resolves it with Claude watching. Requires this folder to be a git clone; for ZIP downloads the fetch fails and nothing happens. --prune drops remote-tracking refs for branches that no longer exist, so a branch renamed on the remote shows up as [gone] in 'git branch -vv' instead of looking healthy. A second hook runs scripts/check_my_branch.py, which is silent when the clone is healthy and otherwise prints exactly what is wrong: sitting on a protected branch, a branch that tracks nothing, a branch whose remote counterpart was renamed away, or a missing repo-local identity. It never blocks.

hooks.command: git fetch origin --prune --quiet && (git merge --no-edit --quiet origin/main || git merge --abort) ; true

hooks.statusMessage: Reading what the team has been doing

hooks._UserPromptSubmit_comment: The team's current state rides along with every question, so Claude cannot take on a piece of research while unaware of what is already claimed. Checking prior art used to depend on a paragraph in CLAUDE.md asking Claude to do it, and a paragraph is a wish rather than a guard. This reads a cache written at session start and never touches the network, so it costs about a tenth of a second and a dozen lines. It prints nothing if the cache is missing or unreadable.
hooks._PreToolUse_comment: Documents are converted to markdown before Claude reads them. A PDF page reaches the model twice, as extracted text AND as a picture of the page, which Anthropic documents at 1,500-3,000 tokens per page; the markdown is the text half alone. This is a hook rather than the markitdown skill because a skill is offered to the model and may not be taken, while a hook runs every time. scripts/convert_for_read.py fails open in every failure case (markitdown missing, scanned PDF with no text layer, encrypted file): it prints nothing and the original read proceeds untouched, because a researcher must never be blocked by a speed optimisation. Each 'if' keeps python from being spawned on reads that are not documents.
hooks._PreToolUse_registration_comment: A finding cannot reach the team without a registration behind it. You cannot mechanically stop somebody running an analysis, and you should not try; what you can do is make the result unshareable until the question was declared. The push is the only moment the whole team is about to be affected, which makes it the one place a refusal is both enforceable and fair. check_registration.py refuses on a definite violation and ALLOWS, loudly, when it cannot check (no upstream, git unavailable, unreadable log): a crashed guard that strands a non-coder mid-push is a worse failure than the one it prevents.
